new_value: Spec decision resolved with evidence: waypoint float fields are canonically 0xfb f64 — pinned by the spec appendix-senml normative independent vector (v:75.0 encoded fb4052c0...), the lichen-senml wire.rs canonical codec policy ('v always encodes as 64-bit floats (0xfb)'), the Python reference (cbor2 defaults), and the committed test/vectors/waypoint.json oracle. The Rust encoder was the outlier: ciborium's deterministic serializer collapses f16-exact floats (10.5 -> 0xf9). Fix: replaced ciborium-serde encoding in Waypoint/WaypointShare/WaypointList to_cbor with a hand-written canonical encoder in waypoint.rs (floats always 0xfb; ints/text shortest-form heads — identical to ciborium's integer behavior; map keys in declaration order with None-skipping identical to the serde skip_serializing_if shape). Decode path unchanged (ciborium accepts all definite widths). Verified: waypoint_vectors byte-exact test now green (2/2, was 1 passed/1 failed), full lichen-client suite green (147+27+17+13+... 0 failed), clippy -p lichen-client --all-features --all-targets -D warnings clean, cargo fmt clean, cargo check clean for all dependents (lichen-apps/cli/tui/sim). The workspace-check failure in lichen-firmware-wio-e5 (duplicate panic_halt lang item) is pre-existing and unrelated (no dep path from lichen-client). 3x reviewer passes (kimi-k3 correctness/security/edge-cases): all PASS; reviewer-verified oracle byte parity for boundary widths (23/24/255/256/65535/65536/2^32) and float values (0.0, 10.5, -430.5). Two pre-existing P3 hardening notes (Waypoint::to_cbor skips validate(); from_reader accepts trailing garbage) filed as new beads. WaypointClientError::Encode is now unconstructible on this path but stays public API (no breaking removal in a lint-fix bead).
